Travelling with Syaha Tour
A journey planned around you, not a fixed departure

Egypt rewards travellers who take their time. Rather than selling set departures, we shape each programme around your travel dates, interests, group size and budget, drawing on detailed planning guides for Cairo and Giza, Luxor, and Aswan and Nubia.

We are honest about the details that matter: which tombs need special tickets, which sites are a separate day away, and which remote temples need advance arrangements. Final visits always depend on current opening hours, site access and ticketing, and every quotation states clearly what is included.

Planning questions
Good to know before you plan
Begin planning your Egyptian journey
Tell us where you would like to go and what you love. We will shape a suggested itinerary and send a tailored quote.
Are these fixed tours with set departure dates?
No. Every journey on this site is a suggested itinerary. We tailor the programme to your travel dates, interests, group size and budget, and confirm it only after checking current access.
Why don't you show prices?

Ticket prices, special tomb access and transport costs change, and they depend on your group and choices. We quote each journey individually after checking current official information, so the figure you receive is one we can stand behind.
What does a quotation include?
Each quotation states clearly what is and is not included: transport, guiding, entrance tickets, meals, boat transfers, accommodation where relevant, optional extras and cancellation terms.
Can you guarantee entry to a specific tomb?
No. In the Valley of the Kings and elsewhere, the tombs open on a given day change for conservation, and some need special tickets. We plan around what is open and treat named tombs as possibilities.
How long is the trip to Abu Simbel?
It is a long day from Aswan, roughly 280 to 300 km each way, and usually around 10 to 12 hours in total. Departure time follows the transport arrangements in force.
Can we visit the Lake Nasser temples in a day?
Usually not. Remote sites such as Amada and Wadi el-Sebua often need a boat or a specialist trip, sometimes with an overnight stay. We arrange them in advance when a route can be confirmed.
We are travelling with children or have limited mobility. Can you adapt?
Yes. We reduce the number of tombs, add rest breaks and check walking distances and drop-off points. Tell us about any needs in the planning form.
Which languages can our guide speak?
Tell us your preferred guide language in the planning form. We confirm guide availability in that language in your quotation.

Cairo & Giza
Cairo
Pyramids, museums and living heritage
Plan Cairo and Giza with Syaha Tour: the Pyramids and Sphinx, the Grand Egyptian Museum, historic and Coptic Cairo, and day trips to Saqqara, Memphis and Dahshur.

Egypt's capital holds five thousand years in a single city. On the Giza Plateau the pyramids of Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure stand beside the Great Sphinx; a few minutes away, the Grand Egyptian Museum gathers the treasures of the pharaohs.

Across the river, the Citadel, the Mamluk mosques of historic Cairo and the lanes of Al-Muizz Street and Khan el-Khalili tell a later story, while the churches of Coptic Cairo sit beside the remains of the Babylon Fortress. Beyond the city, Saqqara, Memphis and Dahshur trace how the pyramids began.
Giza Plateau
The three great pyramids, the Sphinx and the viewpoints between them.
Ancient civilisation, Islamic art and royal palaces.
Historic Cairo
The Citadel, Mamluk mosques and the old bazaar.
Coptic heritage
Churches, a historic synagogue and the Babylon Fortress.
Optional excursions
Earlier pyramids, ancient Memphis, the Nile and the desert.
Begin at the plateau
Start with the panoramic viewpoint to see all three pyramids together, then walk among them with a guide who explains how and why they were built.
Two great museums
Pair the Grand Egyptian Museum with the National Museum of Egyptian Civilization and its Royal Mummies Hall, or the historic Egyptian Museum in Tahrir.
Cairo on foot
Al-Muizz Street is best explored slowly: mosques, madrasas and gates from several Islamic periods, ending among the lanes of Khan el-Khalili.
Separate sites, separate days
Saqqara, Memphis and Dahshur sit outside central Cairo. Allow a full day for them rather than adding them to a Giza visit.
Special tickets
Entering the Great Pyramid, some museum areas and special tombs needs separate tickets with their own rules. We check availability before including them.
Dress and etiquette
Mosques and churches expect respectful dress. Your guide explains visitor rules at each site.
What a quotation covers
Transport, guiding, entrance tickets, lunch, drinks and boat rides are listed line by line, so you know exactly what is included.
Luxor
Temples, royal tombs and ancient Thebes
Plan Luxor with Syaha Tour: Karnak and Luxor Temple on the East Bank, the Valley of the Kings, Hatshepsut's temple and the Nobles' Tombs on the West Bank, with a suggested three-day itinerary.

Luxor is one of the great open-air archaeological landscapes of the world. On the East Bank, Karnak and Luxor Temple are joined by the Avenue of Sphinxes; across the Nile, the West Bank holds the royal tombs and mortuary temples of ancient Thebes.

Most travellers need three days to see it well: one for the East Bank temples and museums, one for the Valley of the Kings and Hatshepsut's temple, and one for Medinet Habu, the artisans' village and a careful choice of Nobles' Tombs.
East Bank
Karnak, Luxor Temple, the Avenue of Sphinxes and two fine museums.
West Bank temples
Hatshepsut, the Colossi, Medinet Habu, the Ramesseum and Deir el-Medina.
Royal tombs
The Valleys of the Kings and Queens, with optional special tickets.
Specialist heritage
Nobles' Tombs and quieter necropolises, subject to access.
Separate excursions
Dendera to the north and Esna to the south.
An unhurried morning at Karnak
The Great Hypostyle Hall, the Sacred Lake and the obelisks deserve time. Allow two to three hours, more if you love archaeology.
Choosing your royal tombs
A standard ticket at the Valley of the Kings covers a selection of tombs. Special tombs such as Tutankhamun and Seti I can be added separately when they are open.
Daily life in paint
At Deir el-Medina and in the Nobles' Tombs, scenes of farming, crafts and ceremonies show how ordinary Egyptians lived.
Crossing to the West Bank
We arrange a vehicle after the river crossing, or a boat crossing linked to local transport, and plan the route to avoid backtracking.
Standard versus special tickets

The standard Valley of the Kings ticket does not include every tomb. Tutankhamun, Seti I and Nefertari may need special tickets, and the selection open changes for conservation. Named tombs are possibilities, not guarantees.
Tombs and heat
Expect steps, narrow passages and hot weather. Comfortable shoes, water and an early start make a real difference.
Restrictions or extra charges may apply at some sites. We check the current rules for your visit.
Hot-air ballooning
Available as an option subject to weather, permits and operator availability. It is never confirmed until the operator does.
Aswan & Nubia
Aswan
Nile islands, Nubian culture and Abu Simbel
Plan Aswan and Nubia with Syaha Tour: Philae, Nubian villages, felucca trips, the Tombs of the Nobles, a full-day excursion to Abu Simbel and specialist Lake Nasser journeys.

Aswan is where the Nile is at its loveliest, flowing between granite boulders and green islands. Philae's Temple of Isis is reached by boat, feluccas drift past Elephantine, and in Gharb Soheil the painted houses of a Nubian village welcome visitors.

South of the city lie the monuments of Nubia: the great temples of Abu Simbel, a long but unforgettable day away, and the temples rescued from Lake Nasser at New Kalabsha. Northbound, Kom Ombo and Edfu make natural stops on the road to Luxor.
Aswan highlights
Philae, the Unfinished Obelisk, the High Dam and the Nubia Museum.
Islands and the Nile
Elephantine, the Botanical Garden, feluccas and the corniche.
Nubian culture
Gharb Soheil, local crafts and optional hospitality.
West Bank heritage
Rock tombs, a desert monastery and the Aga Khan Mausoleum.
Abu Simbel
The temples of Ramesses II and Nefertari, a long day trip.
New Kalabsha
Rescued Nubian temples near the High Dam.
Lake Nasser
Remote temples for specialist journeys.
Northbound
Kom Ombo and Edfu on the way to Luxor.
Philae by boat
The short boat ride to Agilkia Island is part of the experience. Allow two to three hours for the Temple of Isis.
A day in Nubia
Explore Gharb Soheil's architecture and crafts, with optional Nubian hospitality, then return along the river past the islands.
The road to Abu Simbel
A long day of around 10 to 12 hours in total, rewarded by the temples of Ramesses II and Nefertari.
Boats are part of the plan
Philae, the islands and the Nubian villages are reached by boat, with a vehicle for sites on land.
Abu Simbel is a full day
It lies roughly 280 to 300 km from Aswan each way. Departure time follows the transport arrangements and regulations in force.
Lake Nasser needs advance planning

Remote temples such as Amada, Wadi el-Sebua, Dakka and Maharraqa usually need a boat or specialist trip, sometimes with an overnight stay. They are arranged in advance and never sold as an ordinary day tour.
Climbs and heat
Qubbet el-Hawa involves climbing; St. Simeon may involve walking from the boat. Tell us about mobility needs and we will shape the days around them.
Times are estimates
Visit lengths here are planning estimates, not official schedules. Opening hours, tickets and routes are confirmed before booking.
The Pyramids of Giza
The pyramids of Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure, built in Egypt's Fourth Dynasty and still among the most celebrated archaeological sites on earth.
The Great Pyramid of Khufu
Built for King Khufu around the 26th century BC, it was the tallest human-made structure for thousands of years.
Entering the interior needs a separate ticket and depends on site rules and availability on the day.
The Pyramid of Khafre
The second-largest pyramid at Giza. Casing stones surviving near its summit show how smooth the pyramids once looked.
The Pyramid of Menkaure
The smallest of the three main pyramids, surrounded by smaller queens' pyramids and the remains of temples.
The Great Sphinx
A monumental limestone sculpture with a lion's body and a human head, guarding the approach to the pyramid complex.
Panoramic Pyramid Viewpoint
The classic wide view of all three main pyramids, and the best place to understand the layout of the plateau before exploring it.
Grand Egyptian Museum
Near the Giza Pyramids
A major museum of ancient Egyptian civilisation, with monumental galleries and the Tutankhamun collection.
Ticketing may be timed; we check current access when planning your day.
The Egyptian Museum, Tahrir
Downtown Cairo
The historic museum on Tahrir Square, with statues, jewellery, papyri and objects spanning Egypt's ancient periods.
Displays change as collections move between museums; we confirm what is on show.
National Museum of Egyptian Civilization
Fustat, Old Cairo
The story of Egyptian civilisation across its eras. The Royal Mummies Hall is a highlight for many visitors.
Museum of Islamic Art
Bab al-Khalq
One of the great collections of Islamic art: ceramics, metalwork, woodwork, textiles and manuscripts from many regions and periods.
Abdeen Palace Museum
A former royal palace whose museum collections tell the story of Egypt's modern monarchy and state.
Open sections vary; access is confirmed in advance.
Manial Palace Museum
Rhoda Island
A palace complex and gardens blending Egyptian, Ottoman, Persian and European influences.
Cairo Citadel
Islamic Cairo
A fortress begun under Salah al-Din in the 12th century. Its height gives sweeping views of the city, and it holds several historic buildings and museums.
Mosque of Muhammad Ali
Inside the Citadel
Ottoman-style domes and tall minarets make this mosque the Citadel's signature landmark.
Respectful dress is expected; visitor rules are explained on arrival.
Mosque-Madrasa of Sultan Hassan
A monumental Mamluk-era religious and educational complex, remarkable for its scale and stonework.
Al-Rifa'i Mosque
Beside Sultan Hassan, with a grand interior and royal tombs that contrast with the older Mamluk architecture next door.
Al-Muizz Street
A historic street of mosques, madrasas, gates and houses from several Islamic periods, best explored on foot with a guide.
Khan el-Khalili
Cairo's famous traditional market for crafts, lamps, jewellery and cafés, and a lively place to practise polite bargaining.
Coptic Cairo
Old Cairo
A district of churches, religious sites and quiet lanes beside the remains of the Babylon Fortress, at the heart of Egypt's Christian heritage.
We confirm which buildings are open on the day.
The Hanging Church
Built above a gatehouse of the Babylon Fortress, valued for its history, icons and wooden interior.
Ben Ezra Synagogue
Coptic Cairo area
A historic synagogue linked to the celebrated Cairo Geniza documents.
Access arrangements vary and are confirmed locally.
Saqqara and the Step Pyramid
Day trip from Cairo
The Step Pyramid of Djoser is one of Egypt's earliest large stone monuments and a landmark in the story of pyramid building.
Memphis Open-Air Museum
Mit Rahina, day trip
Monumental sculpture and remains from one of Egypt's earliest capitals, usually combined with Saqqara and Dahshur.
Dahshur Pyramids
The Bent Pyramid and the Red Pyramid show how pyramid building developed before Giza.
Nile Felucca in Cairo
On the Nile
A traditional sailboat on the river, most atmospheric around sunset. Duration, departure point and safety arrangements are agreed with the operator.
Wadi Degla Protectorate
Maadi, nature option
A desert canyon on Cairo's edge for walks and striking geology.
Only with suitable transport and water, and with attention to access and weather.
Karnak Temple Complex

One of the largest religious complexes of the ancient world: the Great Hypostyle Hall, the Sacred Lake, obelisks and the Open-Air Museum. The precincts of Khonsu, Mut and Montu lie within or beside it, though not every area is open.
2–3 hours, longer for enthusiasts
A Sound and Light show may run as a separate evening activity; schedule and language are confirmed when booking.
Luxor Temple
Central Luxor
Statues of Ramesses II, courtyards and colonnades built across several reigns, with the Abu Haggag Mosque rising inside the precinct.
1–1.5 hours
An evening visit is lovely when current opening hours allow.
Avenue of Sphinxes
Between Karnak and Luxor Temple
The ceremonial avenue linking the two great temples, lined in sections with sphinx and ram-headed statues. We choose a section that suits your walking time.
Luxor Museum
Corniche, East Bank
A beautifully presented collection of artefacts from ancient Thebes and the Luxor region.
Mummification Museum
How ancient Egyptians embalmed the dead: the materials, the tools and the beliefs behind them.
45–75 minutes
Abu Haggag Mosque
Within Luxor Temple
An important religious landmark built within the Luxor Temple precinct.
Visits respect prayer times and dress guidance.
Luxor Souq and Nile Corniche
Shopping, cafés and riverside walks: an easy-going counterpoint to the temples.
Temple of Hatshepsut
Deir el-Bahari
A dramatic terraced temple set against the cliffs, known for its colonnades and reliefs.
1.5–2 hours
Colossi of Memnon
Theban plain
Two monumental seated statues associated with the mortuary temple of Amenhotep III.
15–30 minute photo stop
Medinet Habu
Temple of Ramesses III
A vast complex with impressive gateways and reliefs of royal and religious life.
The Ramesseum
Mortuary temple of Ramesses II
Courts, historical reliefs and the remains of colossal statues.
Deir el-Medina
Artisans' village
The village and tombs of the craftsmen who built the royal tombs, rich in painted scenes of daily life.
Valley of the Kings
West Bank

The royal necropolis of the New Kingdom pharaohs. A standard ticket covers a selection of tombs; tombs often considered include Ramesses VI (KV9) with its astronomical ceiling, Ramesses III (KV11), Ramesses IV (KV2) and Merenptah (KV8).
2–3 hours

The tombs open on any day change for conservation. Tutankhamun (KV62) and Seti I (KV17) may need a separate special ticket, so they are listed as optional. Expect stairs, narrow passages and heat outside.
Valley of the Queens
Tombs of queens and royal children, including the celebrated painted tomb of Nefertari (QV66) and Amenherkhepshef (QV55).
1–2 hours
Nefertari's tomb is controlled separately and may need a special ticket. Other tombs depend on conservation schedules.
Tombs of the Nobles
Sheikh Abd el-Qurna and Khokha

Tombs of officials, scribes and priests painted with farming, crafts and ceremonies. Candidates include Nakht (TT52), Menna (TT69), Rekhmire (TT100) and Ramose (TT55), and Sennedjem (TT1) at Deir el-Medina.
Half a day for several tombs
Access and tickets vary tomb by tomb. We choose two or three that are open; visiting them all in one tour is not practical.
Asasif Necropolis
An extensive cemetery of tombs from different periods, including the large tombs of high officials.
For specialist tomb-focused tours, subject to access.
Dra' Abu el-Naga
North of the main Nobles' Tombs
An important necropolis that suits travellers who want to go beyond the best-known tombs.
Subject to current access.
Deir el-Shelwit and the Temple of Amenhotep III
Less-visited temples and the remains of Amenhotep III's mortuary temple, with varying levels of preservation.
Included only after we check visitor access and route conditions.
Tod and Armant
South of Luxor
The temple site of ancient Tuphium at Tod and the remains at Armant, for dedicated specialist excursions.
Planned as separate excursions after access is confirmed.
Dendera Temple Complex
Qena Governorate, north of Luxor
A remarkably well-preserved temple dedicated largely to Hathor. It lies outside Luxor and makes a separate day trip.
Esna Temple
The Temple of Khnum, known for its columns and decorated ceiling.
Planned as a separate excursion; opening arrangements are checked first.
Philae Temple
Agilkia Island, by boat
The Temple of Isis, rebuilt on Agilkia Island and reached by a short boat ride.
The Unfinished Obelisk
Granite quarries
An obelisk abandoned in the quarry, revealing how ancient masons cut granite.
45–60 minutes
The High Dam
South of Aswan
A landmark of modern engineering that created Lake Nasser.
30–60 minutes
Entry follows site arrangements on the day.
Nubia Museum
The history, archaeology and living culture of Nubia in one carefully told collection.
Elephantine Island and Aswan Museum
In the Nile at Aswan
The island's archaeological remains, its museum and the ancient Nilometer.
We check which sections are open.
Botanical Garden, Kitchener's Island
By boat
An island garden of varied plants and trees, reached by boat.
Felucca on the Nile
Sail between the islands under a white canvas sail, ideally towards sunset.
Usually 1–2 hours
Aswan Souq and Corniche
The old market and the riverside promenade for shopping, strolling and cafés.
Gharb Soheil Nubian Village
West Bank of Aswan
Colourful architecture, local crafts and Nubian culture, with hospitality available as an option.
Other Nubian islands and villages
Further islands and villages can join a suitable boat route, arranged with a local operator.
Tombs of the Nobles and Qubbet el-Hawa
Rock-cut tombs high above the river, with some of the finest views in Aswan.
Involves a climb and some walking.
Monastery of St. Simeon
A historic Coptic monastery in the desert above the Nile.
Reached by boat, then on foot or by local transport depending on conditions.
Aga Khan Mausoleum
A graceful landmark on the hill above the river, admired from the Nile and its surroundings.
Enjoyed from the Nile and the surrounding area. Interior access is not included or promised.
Roughly 280–300 km south of Aswan
The Great Temple of Ramesses II and the Temple of Nefertari, with time for interpretation and photographs.
A long full day, around 10–12 hours in total
Departure time and route follow the transport arrangements and regulations in force.
Temple of Kalabsha
A temple moved to save it from the rising waters of Lake Nasser.
Access arrangements are checked before we confirm.
Beit el-Wali
A small rock-cut temple associated with Ramesses II.
Visited only where authorised access can be arranged.
Lake Nasser temples
South of the High Dam
Amada, Wadi el-Sebua, Dakka, Maharraqa and other Nubian sites along the lake.

These remote sites usually need an organised specialist trip or a boat, and may involve an overnight stay or several days. They are not an ordinary day tour and are offered only once a route is confirmed.
Kom Ombo Temple
North of Aswan
A distinctive double temple, with the Crocodile Museum beside it. A natural stop on the road to Luxor.
Edfu Temple
North of Kom Ombo
The Temple of Horus, one of the best-preserved temples in Egypt, usually paired with the journey to Luxor.
Pyramids & Grand Egyptian Museum
1 day
The Giza Plateau and the Great Sphinx in the morning, the treasures of the Grand Egyptian Museum after lunch.
The essential first day in Egypt. Begin on the Giza Plateau with the pyramids of Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure, take in the panoramic viewpoint, and stand before the Great Sphinx.
After a lunch break, continue to the nearby Grand Egyptian Museum for its monumental galleries and the Tutankhamun collection.

Saqqara, Memphis & Dahshur
The story of the pyramids before Giza: the Step Pyramid, ancient Memphis, and the Bent and Red Pyramids.
These sites lie outside central Cairo and deserve a full day of their own. At Saqqara, the Step Pyramid of Djoser is among Egypt's earliest monumental stone buildings.
Continue to the open-air museum at Memphis, one of Egypt's earliest capitals, and finish at Dahshur, where the Bent Pyramid and the Red Pyramid show pyramid builders learning their craft.

Luxor in Three Days
3 days
East Bank temples and museums, the Valley of the Kings and Hatshepsut's temple, then Medinet Habu and a selection of Nobles' Tombs.

A balanced first visit to ancient Thebes. Day one stays on the East Bank with Karnak, a museum and an evening at Luxor Temple. Day two crosses the river early for the royal tombs and Hatshepsut's terraced temple.

Day three slows down for Medinet Habu, the Ramesseum or Deir el-Medina, and two or three Nobles' Tombs chosen from those open on the day. Each day is tuned to your energy and interests rather than packed with every site.

Discover Aswan & Nubia in 7 Days
7 days
Aswan's great sites, a day of Nubian culture, Abu Simbel, New Kalabsha, and an optional Lake Nasser or northbound finish.
A week to understand Aswan and Nubia properly. The first days cover Philae, the Unfinished Obelisk, the Nubia Museum, Elephantine and the islands, then a full day of Nubian culture at Gharb Soheil.

The second half travels south: a long day to Abu Simbel, the rescued temples of New Kalabsha, and a day reserved for remote Lake Nasser sites if a specialist trip can be arranged. The final day either heads north via Kom Ombo and Edfu or stays in Aswan.
